$comment: Mod catalogue. One entry per swappable mod asset, keyed by generation where the two cars differ. See mx5-mod-modelling-brief.md §8 for the schema and §7.1 for how `slot`/`optionId` map onto the controls carData.json already defines. `scripts/validate-mod.mjs` reads this file and checks each exported .glb against its entry.
$slots: `slot` is a CarConfig field name and `optionId` an id already present in carData.json's aeroParts/wheelStyles for that slot. A mod with slot:null has no control yet and cannot ship — see brief §7.1.
$anchors: `anchors` names base-asset nodes the mod must reach. blender/anchors.json holds their measured boxes; the validator asserts the exported mod comes within `anchorToleranceMm` of each, which is the machine-checkable form of 'nothing floats'.
$attribution: `derivedFromBaseMesh: true` means the geometry was derived from a CC-BY car asset and ATTRIBUTION.md must record the modification. See brief §4.
$roadmap: What we intend to build, in build order. `mods` is what actually exists; `node scripts/mod-status.mjs` joins the two and says what to pick up next. Everything here is ND-only for now because the NA is not imported into the working .blend.
$origin: `originMm` is the app-space point a mod's geometry is exported relative to. Body mods omit it and ship in absolute app coordinates. Wheels set it to their contact patch, because the app parents them to a pivot already sitting there — see brief §2.2. The validator offsets the bbox by it before checking anchors.

proves the wheel pipeline end to end
quick win, pairs with the bonnets

mods.$note: The boot lid's own rear 260mm, lifted 85mm on a t^2 ramp. Zero slope where it meets the panel, so the front row of vertices is still exactly the boot lid — the brief calls a visible step at the front edge the single most common failure here, and this makes it impossible rather than careful.
mods.$budget: Over the brief's 3000. A panel-derived part inherits the donor's density; the alternative is modelling it freehand, which forfeits the guaranteed shut line. 163 kB, so the cost is bookkeeping rather than performance.

mods.$note: The mild option in the same slot as the ducktail and the wing: 140mm of strip, 35mm rise, with the ends flicking up a little more than the centre so it does not read as a shelf laid across the boot.
mods.$budget: Over the brief's 1500, for the same reason as RA01.

mods.$note: Two hoops 140mm apart with crown spacers and a full-width harness bar at y 950. Both hoops sit inside z -950..-1090, the band where the cabin tub actually offers a surface — outside it the mesh has gaps and a probe returns nothing, which would put footplates at an assumed height.
Built from the same script as EX06 so the pair stay consistent — the brief's warning here is that misaligned twin tips are instantly visible, and two scripts drift.

The oval mouth is a squashed revolve, so the bore stays a real tube rather than a flat plate with a dark decal. Needed a new `twin_oval` id in carData.json — the exhaust catalogue had four and three were taken, and the remaining one is titanium, which this is not.
mods.$partial: Offered on the ND only, because that is the only generation with the asset.

mods.$note: 38mm OD tube, every end on a 100x100x6 footplate at a probed deck height — 797 under the hoop legs, 753 under the stays. Station chosen by probing: at z -820 the cabin mesh is thin over the soft-top well and reports a deck of 853 from one ray height and nothing from any other, so the hoop would have stood on the well cover.
mods.$clash: Occupies the same space as the soft top when the roof is UP — the ND stows its top behind the seats, so this is a roof-down part. Not marked incompatible because the app has no way to express 'requires roof down' yet.

mods.$note: Every plate height is ray-cast from the bonnet at that exact station, so the plates lie on the curved panel rather than hovering at a nominal height — this is a part whose whole job is to look bolted down. Needs the Phase 3 schema extension: CarConfig has no bonnet-hardware field.
mods.$partial: The lanyard is a straight bar; the brief asks for a cable with natural sag.

mods.$note: Sits where the OEM tips MEASURE — app x -354..-220, off-centre to the vehicle's right — not on the centreline the catalogue drawing implies. The tip is a real tube with a separate dark bore sleeve; a solid rod with a dark cap reads as a toy.

Flat and level at app y 150, just under the bumper's measured lowest point of 168, projecting to a leading edge at z 2055 against a nose at 1958. Following the bumper's curve downward instead would make it a valance, which is a different part. Rods run from inside the plate up to y 470, well inside the bumper's 175..644 band, so both ends are buried rather than touching.
mods.$partial: Rods are square-section and vertical; the brief specifies 10mm round and raked back.

mods.$note: Base plates start at app y 858, which is the boot lid's height measured by ray-cast at the upright stations rather than the brief's nominal figure — that assumes a different datum and would leave the uprights hanging. 1400 span against a 1790 cap (body width minus 150). The element is an inverted cambered aerofoil at 8 degrees, trailing edge high.
mods.$partial: No bolt heads on the base plates and no adjuster hardware at the upright/element joint. 320 triangles against a 6000 budget — there is plenty of room to add them.

mods.$note: ET0 puts the mounting face on the centreline, so 114mm of barrel sits outboard of the spoke face — that is the design. The lip is a separate object on MOD_Alloy while the face is MOD_Rim, so the wheel-finish picker recolours the face and leaves the lip polished. 24 exposed bolts, without which a lip this deep does not read as three-piece.
mods.$deviation: The brief lists this as NA-only, but carData.json already offers watanabe_rs on the ND and the NA is not imported into the working .blend, so it is built at 17x9 ET0 for the generation that can show it.

mods.$note: ET25 and genuinely concave spokes — the face is pulled 34mm inboard at the hub and rises to the lip plane at the rim, following (1-t)^1.6. That curve is the design's whole character; flat slabs at constant depth are a different wheel.
mods.$partial: No machined dimple detail near the hub, and the spoke section is a chamfered slab rather than a rounded trapezoid.

mods.$note: Origin is the contact patch, so the app's existing wheel pivot gives it diameter, camber and track for free. Modelled for the LEFT side; place the right-hand instance with rotation.y = PI, which is rigid and so does not flip winding. Outer diameter is 641mm because that is what the ND's wheels measure — building to the 205/45R17 spec instead would shift ride height on every car fitted with it. Ships a caliper, which makes CarConfig.caliperColor live for the first time.
mods.$partial: Spokes are simple tapered slabs. Reads correctly at configurator distance; would want a rounded trapezoid section and machined detail to stand a close-up.

mods.$note: CarConfig has no boot-lid field, so this needs the Phase 3 schema extension before it can ship. Deliberately incompatible with nothing: ducktails and wings still mount to it because their anchors are unchanged. The badge is a separate node and is left alone.

The duct is displaced into the OEM surface rather than cut out of it, so the skin stays continuous; only the throat is a real opening. Its mouth carries a lipped surround because face deletion leaves an edge that follows the panel's topology — see blender/mods/BP03_naca_bonnet.py.

The panel IS the OEM bonnet surface, refined locally around the two apertures and solidified 4mm, so its shut lines and nose edge are correct by construction. Built by blender/mods/BP01_vented_bonnet.py.
